title: Why 12 Monkeys Deserves More Recognition Among 1990s Classics
excerpt:
A retrospective revisits Terry Gilliam's science-fiction classic.
Its time-travel mystery and Brad Pitt's performance remain compelling.
body_md:
Discussions of the greatest films of the 1990s regularly return to Pulp Fiction and The Silence of the Lambs. A retrospective argues that 1995's 12 Monkeys deserves comparable attention.

Bruce Willis plays James Cole, a prisoner sent into the past to investigate a virus that killed 99 percent of humanity. The Army of the Twelve Monkeys is suspected of releasing it, setting up a mystery that challenges the audience's assumptions.

The writer highlights the opening music and the film's willingness to establish atmosphere before plunging into the action. Opening credits and music contribute to its identity.

Brad Pitt's performance as a psychiatric patient receives particular praise, with the writer comparing its manic energy to Johnny Depp in Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas. This is a personal critical reassessment, not a sequel announcement.
